subject: chemistry
question_text: The equilibrium constant for a reaction is 10. What will be the value of ΔG°? (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T = 300 K)

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula and substitution

lines.text: ΔG° = −RT ln K = −2.303 RT log K

steps.why: Standard Gibbs energy and the equilibrium constant are connected by ΔG° = −RT ln K; the factor 2.303 converts the natural logarithm to the base-10 logarithm that log tables use.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign in the formula.
Using 2.303 together with ln — 2.303 belongs with log, not with ln.
steps.memory_tip: K greater than 1 means products are favoured, so ΔG° must come out negative. Check the sign against this before moving on.
steps.margin_note: The formula with values substituted earns this mark, before any arithmetic.

steps.label: The answer with its unit
steps.why: 2.303 × 8.314 = 19.1471, and 19.1471 × 300 = 5744.14, so ΔG° = −5744.14 J mol⁻¹, written here as −5744.1. The source book prints −5774.14 J; that is a digit transposition — the product of these numbers is 5744.14, not 5774.14.
common_mistakes: Copying the book's −5774.14 — the correct product is 5744.1.
Writing the answer without the unit J mol⁻¹.
Losing the minus sign in the final line.
steps.memory_tip: Size check: 19 × 300 is about 5700, so the answer must sit near 5700 J mol⁻¹.
steps.margin_note: Box the signed value with its unit. Both are part of this mark.

insider_note: One substitution and one multiplication — the marks are for the signed value with its unit. The printed key's 5774.14 is a digit transposition: 2.303 × 8.314 × 300 = 5744.14, so this card writes −5744.1 and differs from the printed source. How an examiner marks −5744.1 against a key printing −5774.14 is an open question — no teacher has confirmed it. Write the full substitution line either way: it shows where the product comes from, and it is what the first mark is for.
